summary.name: GNUnet
summary.one_liner: GNUnet is a free software network protocol stack and framework for building secure, distributed, privacy-preserving peer-to-peer applications.
use_cases: research into alternative internet protocol stacks
summary.what_it_does: GNUnet is described as a network protocol stack for building secure, distributed, and privacy-preserving applications. It offers components for addressing, reliable encrypted channels with advanced routing, resource discovery, and naming, intended as a metadata-preserving foundation for applications. The page states it is a self-organizing network and free software, and it says it does not require a public ledger or blockchain consensus. The project says its work is based on research spanning almost two decades.
notable: Metadata-preserving design intended to hide who communicates with whom and when
No public ledger or blockchain consensus, citing sustainability
Free software under GPL-3.0 per the awesome-selfhosted listing
Framework of reusable P2P components for addressing, routing, naming and content distribution
caveats: Page is mostly conceptual and does not name specific supported platforms or installation details
Described as a framework for developers rather than an end-user application
